issues.issue: Unregistered warm-up key. It has no effect on any registered run. Every loader (Stage 0-C, walk-forward by trade slicing, cost stress, the locked test, basket legs read from trades_full_*.parquet) starts at the store's first bar, 2009-12-31. On that market all nine arms produce identical Signals at atr_min_obs 30, 230 and 1000. On a sample that starts after about 2010-03 (a live or MT5 port, a challenge simulation that loads from 2018), the module defines the ATR state on days 49-248, where the oracle leaves it undefined.
issues.fix: No code change. Record in the run notes that any shorter or later-starting run must pass atr_min_obs = 230, or load at least 250 trading days of history before the first traded date.

lookahead_risk: Low; no leak found. ATR20 is F.atr_prev (shifted one day), and the median window ends at the current day's value, which is known at the day's start. On every candidate day the signal bar ei-1 and the entry bar ei fall in the same trading day, so reading the ATR state at ei, as the oracle does, is causal. The VIX percentile at row j uses only rows <= j of the finite subset. It is mapped with F.ext_asof's searchsorted rule and read at the signal bar. ts_avail is always 21:30 UTC, so the 00:55 UTC entry sees the previous US close. I reran Stage 0 on the full pre-holdout market for all nine arms: truncation (cuts at 2016-12-26 13:43 and 2022-08-05 19:57 UTC), perturbation, determinism and 8 release probes all gave 0 mismatches. Later bars are read only by the oracle's inherited guards (ts[ei] within 5 minutes, exit bar exists), which use timestamps, not prices.
notes: (1) Verbatim: 'all' equals the oracle with vol_filter=False, and 'atr' equals it with vol_filter=True, in all 11 Signals fields on the full pre-holdout market (936 and 415 entries). The common sample drops no oracle day from 2011 on. (2) atr_d is NaN only on days 0-19. The oracle's median is first defined on 2010-12-15, on 230 finite values. The module's median equals it on every day the oracle defines it: for i >= w-1 the slices coincide and the finite count is >= w-atr_n >= need. Its 200 extra days run from 2010-03-10 to 2010-12-14, all before start. On the checker sample the module gives 13 entries against 0 under the oracle rule, so the key only makes the leak tests non-vacuous. (3) The 126 null-vix rows are dropped. Every day from 2011 on uses a full 250-close window. An integer reference (V+ iff 2*count(win<=x_j) >= len(win)) reproduces every arm, so the 1e-9 offset flips nothing and V+/V- are strict complements. (4) The both-states-defined check comes before the rule in every arm. The strata are disjoint; their union is 'all'; atr = atr_vix|atr_vixlo; atr_or_vix = atr|natr_vix. No exit falls on a later date. (5) Placebo days are the ~F.is_gotobi weekdays, with the same guards, stop and exit. F.is_gotobi matches an independent calendar. (6) GRID lists the nine arms and vix_pct [50]; the defaults match the spec. vix_pct is plumbed (70: 507 entries, 30: 716, against 613). An unknown state raises. (7) Design 2011-2017: 504/219/83/136/101/184/320/495/822. The extra 2 and 5 days (2011-01-03..11) are there because my expectations used a stricter warm-up that needed 250 finite values (defined from 2011-01-12). The registered oracle loop counts those days, so 184/822 stand, and 504 is the sum of the strata. Check-period counts for K4: 432/196/123/73/97/139/293/561/568. Checker gap: dynamic_check flips state to one value only; I covered all nine arms here. No outcomes were computed.
